name: Question 9
problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=0,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2,\,-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
worked_solution:
First, notice that the unit tangent and the principal normal at the point where $t=0$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡0+\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\ N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the position vector of the point where $t=0$ is

$$
p=r(0)=⟨{e}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,2,\,-{e}^{0}\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩=⟨0,2,-1⟩.
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\times N(0) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our perpendicular vector $n$ is 

$$
n=T(0)\times N(0)=⟨0,-1,0⟩.
$$

Finally, let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ denote the position vector of a point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to $n$ and passes through the tip of the position vector $p$, its Cartesian equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}(⟨x,y,z⟩-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,-1,0⟩ & =⟨0,2,-1⟩\cdot ⟨0,-1,0⟩ \\ x(0)+y(-1)+z(0) & =0(0)+2(-1)+(-1)(0) \\ 0-y+0 & =0-2+0 \\ y-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for the curve r(t) at the point where t=0, given that r(t)=⟨etsin⁡t,2,−etcos⁡t⟩T(t)=12⟨sin⁡t+cos⁡t,0,sin⁡t−cos⁡t⟩N(t)=12⟨cos⁡t−sin⁡t,0,cos⁡t+sin⁡t⟩.

Note that T and N denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.

a
z+1=0
b
x−2y=0
c
x−y−z+1=0
d
y−2=0
e
x+y+z−1=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the unit tangent and the principal normal at the point where t=0 are T(0)=12⟨sin⁡0+cos⁡0,0,sin⁡0−cos⁡0⟩=12⟨1,0,−1⟩N(0)=12⟨cos⁡0−sin⁡0,0,cos⁡0+sin⁡0⟩=12⟨1,0,1⟩.

Also, the position vector of the point where t=0 is p=r(0)=⟨e0sin⁡0,2,−e0cos⁡0⟩=⟨0,2,−1⟩.

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent T(0) and the principal normal N(0): T(0)×N(0)=12⟨1,0,−1⟩×12⟨1,0,1⟩=12ijk10−1101=12[ 0−101i−1−111j+1010k ]=12⟨0,−2,0⟩=⟨0,−1,0⟩

Therefore, our perpendicular vector n is n=T(0)×N(0)=⟨0,−1,0⟩.

Finally, let ⟨x,y,z⟩ denote the position vector of a point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to n and passes through the tip of the position vector p, its Cartesian equation can be written as (⟨x,y,z⟩−p)⋅n=0⟨x,y,z⟩⋅n−p⋅n=0⟨x,y,z⟩⋅n=p⋅n⟨x,y,z⟩⋅⟨0,−1,0⟩=⟨0,2,−1⟩⋅⟨0,−1,0⟩x(0)+y(−1)+z(0)=0(0)+2(−1)+(−1)(0)0−y+0=0−2+0y−2=0.
